title: Slow English Podcast #167: Central African Republic

sentences.text: Today, we will talk about the Central African Republic.
It is a country with forests, wild animals and strong traditions.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is the Central African Republic?
The Central African Republic is in the middle of Africa.
It is next to Chad, Sudan, South Sudan, Cameroon, Republic of the Congo and Democratic Republic of the Congo.
It has no sea, but it has many rivers, forests and savannas.
What is the capital city?
The capital city is Bangi.
Bangi is near the Ubangi River.
It is the largest city in the country.
Bangi has markets, schools, hospitals and government buildings.
Other towns include Bosaingoa, Bambari, Berberati.
How many people live in the Central African Republic?
About five five million people live in the country.
Most people live in villages or small towns.
Some people are farmers, some are herders and many live close to nature.
What language do people speak?
There are two official languages, French, Sango, a national language spoken by most people by her.
People also speak local African languages like Gubaya, Zande and Mangia.
What is the weather like?
The Central African Republic has a tropical climate.
It is hot all year.
The rainy season is from May to October.
The dry season is from November to April.
The north is drier and the south has more rain and forests.
What does the country look like?
The Central African Republic has rain forests in the south, grasslands and bushes in the center and north, rivers, hills and savannas.
It is a land of nature, animals and open space.
What animals live there?
The Central African Republic is home to many animals like elephants, lions and buffalo, gorillas, chimpanzees and monkeys, leopards, antelopes and hippos, birds, crocodiles and snakes.
People visit Zanga Sanga Reserve to see animals in the wild.
What do people eat?
Food is often simple, local and made with what grows nearby.

People eat cassava, a root vegetable made into dough or porridge, maize rice and plantains, peanuts, beans and leafy greens, fish, chicken or goat meat, popular dishes, gozo, cassava dough with sauce, fish stew with tomatoes and onions, fried plantains, peanut soup with vegetables.
People eat together often using their hands.
What do people drink?
People drink water, palm wine, a sweet drink from palm trees, tea, coffee and fruit juice, local beer or drinks made from millet or corn.
What is life like in the Central African Republic?
Life is often traditional, family -centered and close to nature.
People enjoy farming, cooking and walking, helping neighbors, going to church or mosque, dancing, singing and telling stories.
Many people live in mud brick homes with tin or straw roofs.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Independence Day, August 13th, National Day, December 1st, Christmas and Easter for Christians, Eid for Muslims, local festivals with music, drums and dance.
People wear colorful clothes and cook special meals for holidays.
Some fun facts about the Central African Republic.
The flag has blue, white, green, yellow, red and a star.
It is one of the most rural countries in the world.
Pygmy people live in the forests and follow ancient traditions.
Sango is one of the few African languages used by all people.
There are diamonds, gold and wildlife, but the country is still very poor.
Now you know many things about the Central African Republic.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about nature, animals and daily life.
Well done!
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
See you next time.
Goodbye or in Frica, Tini.
